thread.title: Pandora slashes staff, says Oakland is too expensive so it will expand in Atlanta

author: Riley McDermid
title: Pandora slashes staff, says Oakland is too expensive so it will expand in Atlanta
text: – Digital Producer, San Francisco Business Times Feb 1, 2018, 7:33am PST Oakland-based Pandora Media said Wednesday that it will cut 5 percent of its workforce and expand its business in Atlanta, because the Southern city is more cost effective than growing the brand in the East Bay. At the end of June, Pandora said CEO and co-founder of the music streaming service Tim Westergren will step down, as the company retrenches after a massive $480 million infusion from SiriusXM and the sale of its ticketing arm just weeks earlier. Westergren was eventually replaced by Sling TV head Roger Lynch , who has introduced new growth and cost-cutting measures to try to get the struggling media company back on track. Pandora said it estimates that the latest job cuts will save it $45 million annually, adding that Atlanta presents “a significant opportunity to add instrumental talent in a region with lower costs than the company’s headquarters.” “Atlanta is a city with a rich history in music and a large pool of diverse tech talent that we can tap into as we scale,” Lynch said in a statement. “While we are committed to having Oakland remain our headquarters, we’re excited to build on the great foundation of our awesome team there and expand our presence in Atlanta over time.” Pandora's course has been rocky over the last five years. It has introduced multiple layoffs but much of its growth has been hampered by increased competition. The Bay Area Internet-radio company also has attempted to diversify via dealmaking; it bought Ticketfly for $450 million in cash and stock in October 2015 in an attempt to take on competitors Spotify and Apple Music (NASDAQ: AAPL). Over the course of the past four years, shares of Pandora (P:NYSE) have declined nearly 87 percent. On Thursday, the stock gained 4 percent on news of the cost reductions and layoffs.
